# Kosambiya Sutta (MN 48 (PTS MN i 320))

**ID:** MN 48 (PTS MN i 320)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Kosambiya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 320
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosambiya Sutta* (MN 48) is set at Ghosita's Park near Kosambī, where the resident monastic community had fallen into bitter internal dissension, quarrelling and assailing one another with verbal daggers [Granoff; IBC 2011; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995]. In response to this breach of concord, the Buddha intervenes to teach the monks six memorable qualities that create love, respect, and unity, reminding them of the peaceful state they seek [Hazra 1994; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003].

The commentary glosses this *dhammatā* as *sabhāva* ("inherent nature") [Cousins et al. 1974].

The dispute at Kosambī is also well known from the Vinaya literature—such as the Pali *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Vin Kd 10) and the Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda *Kośāmbīvastu*—as well as the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128) [Granoff; Rogell 2003; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse between MN 48 and numerous canonical collections, sharing extensive passages with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10, AN 6, AN 5, AN 4, AN 3), the *Parivāra* (Pvr 4), the *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104), and the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 33, DN 34, DN 16) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus aligns passages of MN 48 with Sanskrit texts (including the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*) and Chinese collections, specifically discourses in the *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
